_transcription: Transcribed 2026-10-30 from render/2026-Physics p01-p19 (p01 cover/instructions: 80 marks, two hours, Section A compulsory, any four from Section B; footer code T26 521). Page map: p02 Sec A Q1(i)-(ii); p03 Q1(iii)-(iv); p04 Q1(v)-(vii); p05 Q1(viii)-(ix); p06 Q1(x)-(xii); p07 Q1(xiii)-(xiv); p08 Q1(xv), Q2(i); p09 Q2(ii)-(iii), Q3(i); p10 Q3(ii)-(vi); p11 Q3(vii), Sec B Q4(i); p12 Q4(ii)-(iii), Q5(i); p13 Q5(ii)-(iii); p14 Q6(i)-(ii); p15 Q6(iii), Q7(i)-(ii); p16 Q7(iii), Q8(i); p17 Q8(ii)-(iii); p18 Q9(i)-(ii); p19 Q9(iii). Numbering check: questions run 1-9 unbroken with Question headers on the pages; Q1 has 15 one-mark MCQs (i)-(xv) under a [15] bracket; Q2 (i)[6]+(ii)[2]+(iii)[2]=10; Q3 (i)-(vi) [2] each + (vii)[3]=15; Section A = 15+10+15 = 40 as printed. Q4-Q9 each (i)[3]+(ii)[3]+(iii)[4]=10; Section B = 6 x 10, attempt any four = 40. No OR alternatives anywhere in the paper. No table of constants is printed; values given inside questions (speed of light, g, speed of sound) stay in their own rows. Q1 instructions are on 1(i) only, the Section B instruction on 4(i) only. 43 rows (Section A 25, Section B 18). Printing oddities kept as printed: 1(x) says 'jars' then 'which tube'; 8(i)(a) prints a stray raised dot after V2 (dropped).

rows.instruction:
SECTION A (40 Marks). (Attempt all questions from this Section.)

Question 1. Choose the correct answers to the questions from the given options. (Do not copy the questions, write the correct answers only.)
rows.text: For a body to be in **dynamic equilibrium,** its:
The energy transformation taking place during **photosynthesis** in plants is:
The **Velocity Ratio** (VR) of a block and tackle system of two pulleys with the **effort** in the **upward** direction is:

rows.chapter: Refraction of Light at Plane Surfaces
rows.subtopic: Laws of Refraction and Refractive Index
rows.text: From the figure given below, the refractive index of medium **B** with respect to medium **A** (\({}_{A}\mu_{B}\)) is:

figure.note: A horizontal boundary with the dashed normal NN' (N at top, N' at bottom). 'Medium B' is labelled above the boundary on the right of the normal and 'Medium A' below it on the left. A ray comes up from the lower right (arrow pointing up-left) making 30 deg with the boundary below it, meets the boundary at the normal and continues up-left making 45 deg with the boundary above it. Options printed with capital 'Sin'.

rows.text: When a blackened bulb thermometer is moved beyond the red region of the visible spectrum, there is a rapid rise in the temperature. This is due to the presence of:
A fast-moving cyclist stops pedalling on reaching a hilly track. If he continues to move with the acquired energy, then assuming **no loss** of energy:
options: his kinetic energy remains constant at all times.
his potential energy remains constant at all times.
his total mechanical energy continuously increases.
his total mechanical energy remains constant.

rows.text: The distance (V) of a virtual image formed by a lens of focal length 15 cm never exceeds a certain **finite** value, then this value will be:
options: less than or equal to 30 cm
less than or equal to 15 cm
rows._flag: The stem does not say which kind of lens (convex or concave); transcribed as printed.

rows.text:
**Assertion (A):** Tiny air molecules **scatter** blue light more than red light.
**Reason (R):** The **refractive index** of a medium is greater for blue light than red light.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.text: In the circuit given below, identify the lamp (\(L_1\), \(L_2\), \(L_3\) or \(L_4\)) whose failure **would not** interrupt the power supply to the other lamps.

figure.note: A cell in the top wire. The left wire runs down through \(L_1\) to a junction; from that junction \(L_2\) runs horizontally across to the right-hand wire; below the junction the left wire continues down through \(L_3\) and then along the bottom wire through \(L_4\) to the right-hand wire, which returns to the cell.

rows.subtopic: Natural and Forced Vibrations and Resonance
rows.text: **Equal** volumes of water are added to three cylindrical jars A, B and C of same height and radii \(r_A\), \(r_B\) and \(r_C\) respectively with \(r_B < r_A < r_C\). If you blow air into the mouth of these jars, which tube will produce the shrillest note?
options: All will produce the notes of same shrillness
rows._flag: Stem calls them 'jars' then asks 'which tube'; transcribed as printed. Subtopic is the closest fit (air-column frequency); could also sit under Characteristics of Sound (pitch).

rows.subtopic: Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity
rows.text: A metallic wire is stretched in such a way that its new length becomes twice the original length. How does its **specific heat capacity** change?
The **correct formula** to calculate the equivalent resistance of two resistors \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) when connected in **parallel,** is:

The diagram below shows the top view of the Wire **A** shown by a cross (**X**), carrying current **into the plane** of the paper. Which of the compasses is **correctly** aligned with the magnetic field, produced by the current carrying wire?

figure.note: Wire A (a circle with a bold X, labelled A) at the centre of a dashed circle. Compass 1 sits on the dashed circle directly above the wire, its needle pointing to the right. Compass 2 sits on the dashed circle to the right of the wire, its needle pointing up.

rows.text:
Three substances A, B and C of **same mass** are present at their respective melting points. On heating, if they melt completely in 5 minutes, 7 minutes and 3 minutes respectively, then which substance has the highest specific latent heat?
*(Assume heat is absorbed at the same rate)*
options: All the substances have same specific latent heat

rows.text:
An atom of lithium contains 3 electrons, 3 protons and 4 neutrons.
Its **mass number** is:

Complete the following by choosing the correct answers from the bracket:
(a) A car is moving in uniform circular motion. The direction of **friction** between the tyres and the path is __________ *[towards the centre / tangential to the path]*.
(b) When a ray of light passes from a **denser to a rarer** medium, its wavelength __________ *[decreases / increases]*.
(c) The **lid** of a calorimeter minimises heat loss by __________ *[convection / radiation]*.
(d) **Quality** of sound depends on its __________ *[amplitude / waveform]*.
(e) A substance whose **resistance** becomes almost negligible at a temperature near **absolute zero** is called a __________ *[semiconductor / superconductor]*.
(f) __________ radiation deviates **minimum** in a magnetic field. *[Alpha / Beta]*.
rows._flag: Six one-mark fill-ins across six chapters (Force, Refraction at Plane Surfaces, Calorimetry, Sound, Current Electricity, Radioactivity); filed under the first. Kept as one row per the ICSE sub-part rule.

rows.text: State *two* factors on which the position of **Center of Gravity** of a body depends.

Case 1: Lata cuts a potato into two halves, using a cutter which belongs to a **Class II** lever. She needed effort \(E_1\).
Case 2: Then she cuts one half of this potato again, but this time she needed effort \(E_2\). If \(E_1 > E_2\) then:
(a) In which case (\(1^{\text{st}}\) or \(2^{\text{nd}}\)) was the potato closer to her hand applying the effort? *(Assume normal reaction of the surface of the potato is same in both cases)*
(b) Give a reason for your answer in (a) above.

The graph below shows the variation of **image distance (v)** with the **object distance (u)** when an object is kept in front of a lens.
(a) Identify the type of **lens** used.
(b) What would be the **magnification** *(more than 1 / less than 1 / equal to 1)* if the object is placed between F and 2F of the above lens?

figure.note: Axes X'X (horizontal) and Y'Y (vertical) crossing at the origin. 'object distance (u)' is labelled along the negative X-axis (X' side) and 'image distance (v)' along the positive Y-axis. A single curve lies in the second quadrant: it starts low near the negative X-axis on the left and rises ever more steeply as it approaches the Y-axis, without touching it. No numbers on the axes.

rows.subtopic: EMF, Terminal Voltage and Internal Resistance
rows.text:
A resistance R is connected across a cell with a switch and a rheostat in **series**. A voltmeter is connected parallel across the **cell**. Current in the circuit is increased using the rheostat.
(a) How will the voltmeter reading change? *(increase / decrease / remain the same)*
(b) Justify your answer stated in (a) above.

rows.subtopic: Natural and Forced Vibrations and Resonance
rows.text:
(a) Define *natural vibrations*.
(b) How is this vibration different from *damped vibrations* in terms of their amplitudes?

rows.subtopic: Heat Capacity and Specific Heat Capacity
rows.text:
A metal piece of **thermal capacity** \(40\ \mathrm{JK^{-1}}\), absorbs 800 J of heat.
Calculate the rise in the temperature of this metal piece.

In an **AC generator**, name the part which has the following functions:
(a) intensifies the magnetic field.
(b) maintains electrical contact between the rotating parts and the external circuit.
Give two differences between **nuclear fission** and **nuclear fusion**.
rows._flag: No taxonomy subtopic names fission/fusion; filed under Nuclear Energy and Safety as the closest.

rows.chapter: Refraction of Light at Plane Surfaces
rows.subtopic: Refraction through a Glass Slab and Prism
rows.text:
A monochromatic ray strikes the surface of identical prisms (**A, B** and **C**) at different angles of incidence. The diagram below shows their refracted rays. Study the path of these refracted rays and identify in which of the diagrams:
(a) the angle of incidence is maximum.
(b) the angle of incidence is minimum.
(c) the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of emergence.

figure.note: Three identical triangular prisms side by side, labelled A, B, C below. Each has a dotted line (normal) at a point on its left face and a refracted ray inside the prism from that point to the right face: in A the refracted ray slopes downward to the right; in B it slopes upward to the right; in C it is horizontal (parallel to the base).

rows.chapter: Refraction of Light at Plane Surfaces
rows.subtopic: Refraction through a Glass Slab and Prism
rows.instruction: SECTION B (40 Marks). (Attempt any four questions from this Section.)
rows.text:
A ray of light enters a glass block from air and comes out from the opposite surface. If the angle of **refraction** at the first surface is **not** the same as the angle of **incidence** at the second surface, then:
(a) What is the product of the ratio \(\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}\) at the first surface and at the second surface?
(b) State whether the opposite surfaces are *parallel* or *not parallel*.
(c) How did you reach the conclusion in (b) above?

rows.chapter: Refraction of Light at Plane Surfaces
rows.subtopic: Laws of Refraction and Refractive Index
rows.text:
A type of glass block has a refractive index of 1.8.
(a) Calculate the speed of light in this glass.
*(Given speed of light in air \(3 \times 10^{8}\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}\))*
(b) If the width of this block is **doubled**, then what will be the speed of light in the block?

rows.chapter: Refraction of Light at Plane Surfaces
rows.text:
(a) Name the electromagnetic radiation used to detect fake currency.
(b) Redraw the diagram given below and complete the path of the light ray **AB** through the glass prism till it emerges out of the prism. Critical angle of the glass is **\(42^\circ\)**.

figure.note: A right-angled glass prism: vertical left face, horizontal base, slanted hypotenuse; right angle at the bottom-left, 30 deg marked at the top vertex. Ray AB travels vertically upward (A below, B on the base, arrow up) and meets the base at B at right angles (perpendicular mark at B), B lying near the right end of the base.

rows._flag: Part (a) is Spectrum (Electromagnetic Spectrum); filed under the diagram part (b).

rows.text:
An object placed in front of a convex lens, forms an image of **same size** on a **screen**. Moving the object 12 cm **closer** to the lens results in the formation of a **real** image which is **three times** the size of the object.
Calculate the *focal length* of the lens.

(a) Atmospheric temperature after a hailstorm is **greater** than the temperature during the hailstorm. State **True** or **False**.
(b) Which **thermal physical quantity** of a frying pan changes by making its base heavier?
(c) State the principle of Calorimetry.
rows._flag: Spans three Calorimetry subtopics: (a) Latent Heat, (b) Heat Capacity, (c) Principle of Calorimetry; filed under (c).

rows.text:
The given graph represents the **cooling curve** of a liquid.
(a) State the freezing temperature of the liquid.
(b) Name the phase change happening at the region QR.
(c) In which state *(solid / liquid)* does the above substance liberate heat at a faster rate? Justify.

figure.note: Graph on a square grid. Vertical axis 'Temperature (\(^0\)C)' marked 10, 20, 30, 40, 50; horizontal axis 'time(s)' marked 5, 10, ..., 35, origin labelled (0,0). Straight-line segments: P (0 s, 50) down to Q (20 s, 20); Q to R (30 s, 20) horizontal; R down to S (35 s, 0).

rows.text:
The diagram shows a wheel with a handle. Two forces, \(\mathbf{F_1}\) and \(\mathbf{F_2}\) of **equal magnitudes** are acting on the handle as shown in the diagram.
(a) Which force produces **negative** moment?
(b) Is the wheel in **equilibrium**? *(Yes or No)*
(c) Justify your answer stated in (b).

figure.note: A wheel with centre O; dashed horizontal and vertical diameters; the upper vertical radius is labelled r. A handle runs from O up and to the left, its end outside the wheel. At the handle's end, \(F_1\) acts vertically upward (its line drawn from the extended horizontal dashed line through O, to the left of the wheel) and \(F_2\) acts horizontally to the left along the line tangent to the top of the wheel (at height r above O).

rows.text:
(a) Name the unit of work done, used in **subatomic** scale.
(b) To which class of lever does a **pair of scissors** belong?
(c) A stone is tied to a string and displaced from **A** to **B** by application of constant force **F** in three different ways as shown in the diagram below. Arrange the three cases in **ascending order** of the work done by the force. *(Given AJB is a semi-circle, \(\theta < 90^\circ\) and AB = 20 m)*

figure.note: Three boxed panels. Case 1: a stone at A is moved along a dashed semicircular path A-J-B (J at the top, arrows along the arc); a force F is drawn from the stone pointing down-right towards the line AB. Case 2: the stone moves along the straight dashed line A to B with F horizontal, along AB. Case 3: the stone moves along the straight dashed line A to B with F at angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal.

rows._flag: Part (b) is Machines (Levers); filed under Work for (a) and (c).

rows.text:
A ball of mass 20 g falls from a height of 45 m. It rebounds from the ground to a height of 40 m. Calculate:
(a) the initial potential energy of the ball.
(b) the speed of the ball at which it hits the ground.
(c) the loss in kinetic energy on striking the ground.
*[\(g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}\)]*

To lift a load of 30 kgf, Suhas uses a single fixed pulley, while Radha uses a single movable pulley. The **displacement of efforts** in both the cases are **equal**. In an **ideal situation** calculate the ratio of:
(a) the efforts in the two cases.
(b) the potential energy gained by the loads in the two cases.
(c) the efficiencies in the two cases.

rows.subtopic: Natural and Forced Vibrations and Resonance
rows.text:
(a) One end of a plastic foot ruler is held tightly at the edge of a table and the other end is plucked. Name the vibrations produced in the ruler.
(b) Now the ruler is pushed inside partially and plucked again from its free end. State **with a reason** whether the frequency of vibration increases or decreases.

Two persons **A** and **B** are standing in front of a cliff in the same line 170 m apart as shown in the diagram. Person **B** fires the gun and hears the echo in 3 s. Then the person **A** standing in front of the person **B** fires the gun.
*(The speed of sound in air is 340 m/s.)*
(a) Calculate:
1. the distance of the person **B** from the cliff.
2. the **minimum** time in which **B** hears the gunshot fired by **A**.
(b) *Fill in the blank.* The echo is softer (less loud) than the original sound due to the **decrease** in __________ of the wave. *(amplitude / frequency)*

figure.note: A boxed sketch: a cliff at the left end of a ground line; person A stands on the line some way to the right of the cliff and person B further right, both holding guns; a double-headed dashed arrow between A and B is labelled 170 m. B is farther from the cliff than A.

rows.text:
Bulb **A** rated 160 W, 40 V and Bulb **B** rated 40 W, 40 V are connected as shown in the diagram.
(a) Calculate the ratio \(V_1 : V_2\).
(b) If the bulb **A** fuses, the current in the circuit remains the same.
State **True** or **False**.

figure.note: Bulb A (labelled 160 W, 40 V) and bulb B (labelled 40 W, 40 V) connected in series in the top wire of a loop closed by a 40 V cell in the bottom wire. Voltmeter \(V_1\) is connected across bulb A and voltmeter \(V_2\) across bulb B.

rows.text:
The reverse side of a three-pin plug with **incorrect** connection of wires is shown in the diagram below.
(a) Identify the **fault** in the above *connection*.
(b) Mention a risk factor involved, if the user operates the appliance without correcting it.
(c) Will the appliance function in the present situation? *(Yes or No)*

figure.note: Photograph of the inside of a three-pin plug, cable entering at the bottom. Labels: 'red wire' points to the wire at the top (large) terminal; 'blue wire' points to the wire at the left terminal; 'green wire' points to the wire at the right terminal. Greyscale photo, so the colours are known only from the labels.

rows.text:
In the combinations of resistors shown below, calculate:
(a) the resistance across AB when the switch **S is open**.
(b) the resistance across AB when the switch **S is closed**.

figure.note: Between terminals A (left) and B (right), two parallel branches: the upper branch has \(12\ \Omega\) then \(6\ \Omega\) in series; the lower branch has \(6\ \Omega\) then \(12\ \Omega\) in series. A switch S joins the midpoint of the upper branch (between \(12\ \Omega\) and \(6\ \Omega\)) to the midpoint of the lower branch (between \(6\ \Omega\) and \(12\ \Omega\)).

rows.text:
An electric iron rated 1100 W, 220 V is operated for 5 hours.
Calculate:
(a) the **minimum** rating of the fuse required.
(b) the energy consumed in **kWh**.
(c) the cost of the energy consumed, if the rate is ₹ 10 per unit.
rows._flag: Part (a) (fuse rating) touches Household Circuits (Fuses, Switches and Earthing); filed under Electrical Energy and Power for (b) and (c).

rows.text:
When the magnet as shown in the diagram, is moved towards the coil at a speed of \(5\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}\), the galvanometer shows a certain deflection to the right.
How will the **direction** and **magnitude of deflection** change when the **coil** also moves with a speed of \(5\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}\):
(a) in the direction of the motion of the magnet?
(b) in the opposite direction of the motion of the magnet?

figure.note: Boxed sketch: a coil wound on a horizontal core, its ends joined through a galvanometer G below it; arrows at G labelled 'Left' (pointing left) and 'Right' (pointing right). To the right of the coil, a bar magnet N S with N facing the coil; an arrow pointing left (towards the coil) labelled 'Movement of magnet'.

rows.text:
(a) 1. Which **element** is used in the lining of the special aprons worn by workers in nuclear power plants?
2. Why is this element preferred?
(b) \({}^{24}_{11}\mathrm{Na}\) emits a nuclear radiation which **does not alter** the mass number but is **deflected** by a magnetic field.
1. Name the type of nuclear radiation emitted by \({}^{24}_{11}\mathrm{Na}\).
2. Write the equation for this radioactive decay.
rows._flag: Part (a) is Nuclear Energy and Safety (protective aprons); filed under Alpha, Beta and Gamma Emissions for (b).
